concepts.title: Law and Justice: Why Courts Matter

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Law and Justice: Why Courts Matter' refers to.
questions.a: The judiciary exists to settle disputes and deliver justice - because injustice anywhere threatens justice everywhere, an independent court system hears both sides, applies the law without fear or favour, and shields the weak against the powerful.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Law and Justice: Why Courts Matter'.
questions.a: Courts turn written law into lived justice through fair, independent hearings.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Law and Justice: Why Courts Matter' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: hees204.txt lines 5-74 (role of the judiciary, connection between law and justice))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Structure of Courts in India' refers to.
questions.a: India runs an integrated judicial system - a single pyramid from district courts at the base through high courts of the states up to the Supreme Court of India at the apex, so any ruling can be appealed upward under one uniform framework.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Structure of Courts in India'.
questions.a: One pyramid of courts: district to high court to Supreme Court, all connected.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Structure of Courts in India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: hees204.txt lines 143-190 (courts in India, judicial system, Supreme Court))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Jurisdictions of the Supreme Court' refers to.
questions.a: The Supreme Court holds several powers: original jurisdiction to decide centre-state disputes directly, appellate jurisdiction to hear appeals from lower courts, and writ jurisdiction to protect fundamental rights by issuing writs like habeas corpus.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Jurisdictions of the Supreme Court'.
questions.a: Dispute-settler, court of appeals and rights-guardian: the three roles of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Jurisdictions of the Supreme Court' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: hees204.txt lines 187-260 (writ, original and appellate jurisdiction))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Judicial Review and Public Interest' refers to.
questions.a: Through judicial review the courts can strike down laws and government actions that violate the constitution, and through public interest litigation even a letter or email from any concerned citizen can open the court's doors for the disadvantaged.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Judicial Review and Public Interest'.
questions.a: Courts keep the constitution supreme and open their doors to all through PIL.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Judicial Review and Public Interest' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 4 (source: hees204.txt lines 260-360 (judicial review, public interest litigation))
